I thought it might help to talk to someone about it, if that makes sense.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe for certain that the property manager and your neighbors are deliberately trying to force you out?\n\nPatient: I mean… “for certain” is a strong way to put it, and I don’t want to sound unreasonable. But yes, I do believe it’s deliberate. It’s been going on for months — the mail being sent to the wrong place, the noises in the walls happening at these specific times, and then neighbors making little comments that seem to connect to it.\n\nThey’ve given me paperwork and explanations, and I’ve tried to consider those, really. But the pattern is still there. I can see it, and it feels very much like they’re trying to pressure me out of the apartment.\n\nDoctor: Have you heard voices when no one was actually there?\n\nPatient: No, I don’t think so. I mean, I hear noises sometimes, like I mentioned, but not voices talking to me when nobody’s there. At least… not that I’d describe it that way. Does that make sense?\n\nDoctor: During this time, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?\n\nPatient: I wouldn’t say depressed most of the day nearly every day, no. I mean, I’ve been stressed and worn down by all of this, certainly, but “depressed” feels… maybe stronger than what I’d call it. I’m still getting through my days. Does that answer what you’re asking?\n\nDoctor: Have you had the feeling that someone can control your thoughts?\n\nPatient: No… I don’t think so. I’ve never felt like someone was actually controlling my thoughts. I can get preoccupied with what’s going on, sure, but my thoughts still feel like mine. Is that what you mean?\n\nDoctor: Have you found yourself withdrawing from other people or losing interest in things you usually care about?\n\nPatient: A little, yes… though I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’ve just stopped functioning. I’ve pulled back from a few consulting jobs, and I’m not painting as much as I usually would. A lot of my week gets taken up following up with neighbors, offices, building staff—trying to get things sorted out. So I suppose I have withdrawn some, yes. Is that the kind of thing you mean?\n\nDoctor: Do you believe there is a hidden system or conspiracy in the building specifically organized to force you out?\n\nPatient: Well… “conspiracy” sounds a bit dramatic, and I don’t want to come across as unreasonable. But yes, I do think there’s a system to it. For months now, the property manager and certain people in the building have been… using things like misdelivered mail, noises in the walls at very specific times, little comments from neighbors—small things, but they line up too neatly.\n\nIt feels organized to pressure me out of the apartment. And I know they have paperwork and explanations for each piece of it, but those don’t really change the pattern I’m seeing. Does that make sense?\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so other people could know what you were thinking?\n\nPatient: No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had the sense that my thoughts are going out where people can hear them or know them. My thoughts still feel private, if that’s what you’re asking.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever believed that an outside force was sending you special messages through the television, radio, or internet?\n\nPatient: Not exactly through television or radio, no. I don’t want to overstate it. It’s more… in the building itself. The misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls that happen at particular times, and certain comments from neighbors—it feels like those are the messages, or signals, I suppose.\n\nI know that may sound like I’m reading too much into things, but after months of it, the pattern is hard to ignore. Their paperwork and explanations don’t really account for how it all lines up. Does that make sense?\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed your emotions feeling noticeably flatter or less expressive than usual?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so, no.
